facts.raw_span: multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules located on the face and vulva
The lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased to approximately 60 lesions
Medical history was significant for a meningioma
Family history was notable for a daughter with similar facial papules that had not undergone biopsy
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Radiographic studies did not reveal any jaw cysts
A conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene (c.757-2A>G) in all tumor and normal tissue samples
Additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples
No deletions present in the normal sample

concepts.why: The presence of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules, histopathological findings of buds and cords of basaloid cells, and a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene support this diagnosis.
The histopathological findings of buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces are characteristic of this diagnosis.
The presence of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules and histopathological findings of buds and cords of basaloid cells support this diagnosis.
The family history of similar facial papules and the presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene support this diagnosis.

The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene and the absence of deletions in the normal sample support the diagnosis of Gorlin syndrome, which is characterized by multiple basal cell carcinomas and other tumors.

rationales.F01: Multiple dome-shaped papules are characteristic of Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome and Familial multiple basal cell carcinoma.
rationales.F03: Meningioma is associated with Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.
rationales.F04: Family history of similar facial papules suggests a genetic component, supporting Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome and Familial multiple basal cell carcinoma.
rationales.F06: Histopathological features of buds and cords of basaloid cells are typical of basal cell carcinoma and its variants.
rationales.F09: SUFU gene mutation is a strong indicator of Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.
rationales.F10: Additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in tumor samples support Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome and Familial multiple basal cell carcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, family history of similar lesions, and association with meningioma support the diagnosis of Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome, despite the absence of some typical features like palmar or plantar pits and jaw cysts.
